From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Aug 2024 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: POC onramp plan & environment gating (API keys, org, IP allowlist, VPC)

Alex / HealthBound team —

Following up from Tuesday's demo, attached is a compact Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on the technical onramp for the POC. The goal is to get a production-like tenant and connectivity in place so your QA and ML team can run realistic traffic next week. High-level items I included:

- Org & tenant seed: service accounts and RBAC roles we recommend
- API keys: ephemeral key pattern + rotation guidance
- IP allowlist: minimal egress/IPs to open for our hosted lane
- VPC peering checklist: template and expected calendar (3 business days once peering request accepted)

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm the primary technical contact for VPC/peering (network) and a procurement point of contact for the small MSA addendum.
2) We schedule a 30-min kick-off to walk the MAP and assign owners (I put proposed owners in the attached MAP_HB-v1.xlsx).
3) HealthBound approves the initial IP ranges and provides an estimate for SLA/test windows.

Attachments: MAP_HB-v1.xlsx (MAP workbook), Redwood-SOC2-summary.pdf (compliance snapshot), vpc-peering-template.txt (peer request template).

If we lock these items by Friday your team can have an environment seeded and an API key within 48h of the kick-off.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0143

Marcus —

Thanks for the MAP and attachments. Looks sensible. Quick answers:
- Primary network contact: Priya Rao (priya.rao@healthbound.com) — looping her on this thread separately.
- Procurement: procurement@healthbound.com (copying). They will need an estimated SOW and payment terms to process the credit card hold.
- Timeline: we can confirm IP ranges by EOD Friday; peering window may need internal approval (our security reviews typically take 48–72h).

Couple of technical Qs for Neha / Ben:
1) For ephemeral API keys — can you confirm token TTL and recommended rotation cadence?
2) For VPC peering — do you require route propagation or will a static route suffice?

If we can have a 30-min walkthrough tomorrow at 10am PT that would help the network team.

Alex / Priya —

Thanks — joining Priya here. 10am PT tomorrow works for us; I booked a tentative 30-min slot and added a link in the HubSpot activity (see related link). Agenda: MAP walk (10min), VPC peering template review (5min), API key provisioning & TTL (10min), next steps/owners (5min).

Quick answers to your questions so Neha/Ben can add detail during the call:
- Ephemeral API keys: default TTL = 24 hours for POC; we can issue a long-lived API key scoped to read-only telemetry for your non-prod tests if needed. Rotation cadence: daily for ephemeral, weekly for scoped long-lived keys.
- VPC peering: static routes are fine for the typical hosted-to-VPC peer. If your infra uses dynamic propagation we can accept that too; the template includes both sets of instructions.

Neha, Ben — can you confirm whether Redwood needs any additional CIDR approvals (beyond the three ranges in the attached MAP sheet) before we ask HealthBound to open the allowlist?

Marcus
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Rao <priya.rao@healthbound.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@healthbound.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 03 Aug 2024 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: POC onramp plan & environment gating (API keys, org, IP allowlist, VPC)

Priya / Alex —

Great to meet this morning. Following up with the technical checklist and a few clarifications so your networking and security teams have everything to hand:

1) CIDR approvals: The three ranges in MAP_HB-v1.xlsx are the only ones we need opened for the hosted POC lane. Confirming we do NOT need 0.0.0.0/0.
2) VPC peering template: please use vpc-peering-template.txt; if your cloud team prefers a ticket-based intake we can accept a PDF export of the same fields. Expected turnaround: once HealthBound submits the peering request we estimate 48 business hours to complete peer validation from our side.
3) API key options:
   - Short-lived (recommended for POC): 24h TTL, rotated automatically by our control plane.
   - Scoped long-lived (for load testing): 7-day TTL with IP restrictions and read-only scopes (we will log usage).
4) Security deliverables: Redwood-SOC2-summary.pdf attached. If procurement needs the full SOC 2 report we can start a secure upload; procurement@redwood.ai will receive the doc on request.

Attachments: MAP_HB-v1.xlsx, vpc-peering-template.txt, Redwood-SOC2-summary.pdf.

Next steps:
- Priya to submit peering request (use template) and confirm network contact.
- Procurement to confirm PO path and whether a short MSA addendum is required for the reserved test credits.

If anything urgent pops up, ping me directly — Neha (slack: @nkapoor).

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
